Former Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp has launched a strong criticism of FIFA president Gianni Infantino, claiming that football’s governing body needs new leadership and suggesting that things have become worse under him than during Sepp Blatter’s tenure. Blatter resigned as FIFA president in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016. However, Infantino has recently faced growing criticism over his proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which included selling stakes in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. As reported by BBC Sport on Monday, speaking about the controversy, Klopp said he believed a change of leadership at FIFA would be beneficial to world football. “I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The former Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool manager added that FIFA needed someone new to take charge. “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job,” he said. Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council over the FFE proposal but has faced calls to release all relevant documents and answer questions surrounding the plan. Diallo received unanimous support from UEFA’s executive committee, with formal ratification from the French Football Federation expected on Tuesday. UEFA has repeatedly criticised Infantino’s leadership and called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community. Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who serves as FIFA’s head of global development, had reportedly considered challenging Infantino but has decided against entering the race. Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima have also expressed interest in contesting the presidency. Klopp believes FIFA needs a leader whose priorities go beyond financial interests. “There are people who truly care about the future of football – people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” he said. “If someone like that were to step up – if someone like that were to become president – I think that would be a significant improvement. “There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.” Gilbert Ekugbe Gilbert Ekugbe is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over a decade of experience reporting on business and economic affairs.
